flashcards.q: Which Functions plan is the default choice in 2026 and when did it GA?
flashcards.a: Flex Consumption - GA November 2024; Linux-only, scale-to-zero, per-instance concurrency, per-function scaling, VNet support, up to 1000 instances.
Linux Consumption: no new features/language versions. Windows Consumption retires September 30, 2028. Max 200 instances, ~1.5 GB fixed memory.
~230 seconds - the Azure Load Balancer idle timeout; functionTimeout cannot extend it. Use Durable async pattern (202 + status URL).
Consumption: 5 default / 10 max minutes. Flex/Premium/Dedicated/Container Apps: 30 min default, unbounded configurable (60-min scale-in grace, 10-min platform-update grace).

flashcards.q: Flex instance sizes and default HTTP concurrency?
flashcards.a: ~512 MB / 2048 MB / 4096 MB instances; HTTP concurrency defaults 4 / 16 / 32 respectively - Python defaults to 1 until configured.
Pre-provisioned warm instances billed flat as provisioned memory regardless of invocations; eliminate cold starts for their share of traffic; don't count toward max instance count.

flashcards.q: Why must Flex blob triggers use Event Grid source?
flashcards.a: It's the only supported blob source on Flex; legacy polling trigger adds up to ~10-minute latency plus storage transaction costs on churny containers.

flashcards.q: What happens after MaxDequeueCount failed attempts?
flashcards.a: Message moves silently to <queue>-poison queue (default 5 attempts); delivery is at-least-once so handlers need idempotency; monitor poison depth.

flashcards.q: Why must orchestrator code be deterministic?
flashcards.a: Orchestrators REPLAY from history on every resume; non-deterministic calls (datetime.now, random, I/O) diverge replays and corrupt workflows. Activities do real work; use context time only.
50 on Consumption plan, 5000 on other plans; entities are single-threaded actors serializing access per entity.

flashcards.q: Task hub storage providers on Flex?
flashcards.a: Only Azure Storage provider (queues+tables+blobs, throughput ceiling) or Durable Task Scheduler (managed, Event Hubs-partitioned) - the high-throughput recommendation.

Consumption ~$0.20/M executions + ~$0.000016/GB-s with free grants; Flex bills execution time (1000 ms minimum billable, rounds per 100 ms) + always-ready memory; Premium = core-seconds floor, no execution charge.

flashcards.q: Does Azure Functions have a SnapStart equivalent?
flashcards.a: No snapshot-restore across runtimes like AWS SnapStart; mitigation is small packages, deferred init, Premium prewarmed or Flex always-ready instances.

flashcards.q: What does the Functions scale controller watch?
flashcards.a: Event lag/depth at the source (not CPU); Flex computes desired instances = events / configured concurrency bounded by a scale curve that throttles bursts at high instance counts.
